title: OpenAI-compat: deterministic tool resolver and streaming-fragment boundary fixes
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Users of the OpenAI compatibility layer have observed intermittent failures when the model emits tool invocations across streaming fragments, and ambiguity when multiple candidate tools are suggested by the model. This PR introduces a deterministic 'tool resolver' and a streaming-framing repair for tool invocation messages so that downstream parsers and tool adapters receive a single, canonical invocation envelope. Motivation: reduce production errors where a tool call is split across fragments (parser errors and duplicate invocations) and to make the 'tool_choice' semantics explicit and consistent with OpenAI-style tool calling while mapping to Redwood's internal tool registry.
commits: feat(tool-resolver): implement deterministic resolver with priority heuristics (late-binding, name + signature match)
fix(streaming): coalesce tool invocation frames and emit dedicated 'tool_invoke_complete' event before handler dispatch
chore(tests): add fuzz tests for fragmented tool_call JSON and multiple-candidate tool responses
docs(openai-compat): document new x-rw-schema annotations and resolver rules
review_comments: Diego Moreno: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) make the resolver deterministic across identical name collisions by preferring exact param schema match, (2) add a telemetry counter for 'fragmented_tool_invocations' — addressed in second commit.

Asha Patel (author): Added deterministic tie-breaker (schema similarity score) and emitted 'fragmented_tool_invocations' metric. Also added an exponential backoff debounce to avoid double dispatch on re-ordered fragments.

Lina Zhou: Integration tests look good. One question about security — what happens if an unknown tool name arrives? We should not auto-invoke. — added explicit fallback to 'user_confirm' mode; no silent invocation.
Owen Park: Tested with the streaming harness (perf-canary) and saw no increase in median latency; added a small benchmark in the PR notes. Approving.
CI bot: initial job failed on lint (stream_coalescer.ts) due to unused import; fixed in a follow-up commit. Final CI: all checks passed.
release_notes: Stabilize OpenAI-compat tool calling: canonicalize tool invocation messages across streaming fragments; deterministic resolver for multiple-candidate tool responses; explicit unknown-tool fallback to user confirmation; added telemetry for fragmented invocations; no breaking changes.
notes_and_testing: Added unit and integration tests: fragmented JSON reassembly, resolver tie-breaker cases, unknown-tool fallback
Canary: deployed to perf-canary with 24h of traffic; observed 0 parser errors for tool invocations vs baseline 0.8%
Rollout plan: staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on spike in 'tool_invocation_errors' metric
